children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures incurred sharp losses, following the Chicago soy complex to the downside.
There were steep declines in soyoil Wednesday along with more moderate reductions in soybeans and soymeal. European rapeseed was down as well, but Malaysian palm oil moved higher.
Crude oil turned around to add stronger increases, but not nearly as hefty as Tuesday. The spillover helped temper the decreases in the vegetable oils.
An analyst said soyoil remaining above 70 cents per pound is good for canola prices.
Despite canola's reversal, its November contract remained well above its major moving averages.
Canola crush margins eased a little with the November positions between C$284.20 to C$291.20 per ton above the futures.
Manitoba reported its canola harvest reached 5% complete and the overall provincial harvest was at 11% done.
The Canadian dollar was stronger, jumping to 72.25 U.S. cents, compared to Tuesday's close of 71.96.
There were 68,404 canola contracts traded on Wednesday, compared to 80,659 on Tuesday. Spreading accounted for 33,518 contracts traded.
